# Margin Control Tower

Status: dual-source, browser-native analytics case study. The committed Olist-derived Parquet
artifact is requested by default. The browser verifies its exact bytes and linked reports, renders
a compact preview, then—after the scheduled eight-second warm or an earlier qualifying
interaction—registers a copy of those same verified bytes with DuckDB-WASM and activates the full
dataset. If the real artifact is absent, malformed, or fails its browser contract, the UI fails
closed and keeps the separately labeled fixed-seed synthetic fallback active.

## Decision workflow

A category manager selects a week, category, mapped region, and channel; reconciles the margin
bridge; compares cost drivers; and tests a bounded scenario without presenting that scenario as a
forecast or causal result.

## Synthetic fallback

`synthetic-margin-data.json` and CSV are generated by `npm run generate:analytics` with fixed seed
`2026071301`. They contain 9,360 fictional rows across 52 weeks, 20 products, five categories,
three regions, and three channels at `week x product x region x channel`. The final eight weeks are
a disjoint synthetic holdout. Every row is tagged `provenance=synthetic`; no external dataset
license or real commercial result is claimed for this fixture.

## Committed real artifact

Real mode loads [olist-margin.parquet](olist-margin.parquet), a 15,809-cell ZSTD aggregate derived
from the public Olist Brazilian e-commerce dataset: 99,441 source orders and 112,650 order-item
rows reconciled with customer state, payments, reviews, order status, product category, and
freight. Its grain is `week x product_category x mapped region x dominant payment channel`; it is

Real mode loads [olist-margin.parquet](olist-margin.parquet), a 15,809-cell ZSTD aggregate derived
from the public Olist Brazilian e-commerce dataset: 99,441 source orders and 112,650 order-item
rows reconciled with customer state, payments, reviews, order status, product category, and
freight. Its grain is `week x product_category x mapped region x dominant payment channel`; it is
not product-level evidence.

- Authority: [Olist on Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce)
- Retrieval date: 2026-07-17
- License: [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/)
- Pipeline: [reproduction and locked inputs](../../../pipelines/olist-margin/README.md)
- Provenance: [source, transport, attribution, and output hashes](../../../pipelines/olist-margin/PROVENANCE.md)

Raw Olist rows are not committed. The browser downloads the Parquet once, computes SHA-256 over
those exact bytes, registers a copy of those same verified bytes with lazy DuckDB-WASM, and renders
[detection-report.json](detection-report.json) and
[elasticity-report.json](elasticity-report.json) only when each report names the identical hash.
The final eight observed weeks must be the only holdout weeks, with no week crossing splits.

## Measurement and proxy boundaries

- Item price and freight are observed after payment/review reconciliation.
- The discount proxy uses a shifted, expanding category-median reference price. A category's first
  observation has no prior history, so it explicitly falls back to current price and produces zero
  proxy discount for that cold-start observation.
- Returns are a disclosed order-status/review proxy; COGS is a disclosed 60% item-price proxy.

- The discount proxy uses a shifted, expanding category-median reference price. A category's first
  observation has no prior history, so it explicitly falls back to current price and produces zero
  proxy discount for that cold-start observation.
- Returns are a disclosed order-status/review proxy; COGS is a disclosed 60% item-price proxy.
- Before STL, 95 observed totals are reindexed to the complete 106-Monday calendar; the 11 Mondays
  with no derived Olist cell are explicitly zero-filled. The detector evaluates six deterministic
  perturbations only on observed Mondays. Calendar-completion rows and replay labels never enter
  the Parquet, and no manually labeled real anomaly is claimed.
- The log-log price coefficient is fit on the analysis window. The later eight-week holdout is used
  only to evaluate MAPE; the estimate is associational, not causal.

The generated [methods evidence](methods-evidence.json) contains bilingual acquisition, cleaning,
split, modeling, label, metric, reproduction, and claim-boundary disclosures. This case study does
not claim audited company economics, causal lift, a forecast, or production decisioning.

chunks.content:
# Credit Policy Lab

Status: dual-source, deterministic policy/backtest case study. The committed scored Lending Club
artifact is requested by default. Missing or invalid real bytes fail closed and leave the
separately labeled fixed-seed synthetic fallback active.

## Decision workflow

A credit policy manager compares baseline and challenger PD, applies approval/review thresholds,
computes expected loss from disclosed PD/LGD/EAD inputs, manages review capacity, and records a
policy decision. Model scores, economics, policy, human review, and audit remain separate stages.

## Synthetic fallback

`synthetic-credit-data.json` and CSV are generated by `npm run generate:analytics` with fixed seed
`2026071302`. They contain 12,000 fictional applications across 12 synthetic vintages with explicit
train/calibration/backtest splits, generated outcomes, deterministic scores, no PII, and no
external credit records. The fixture is covered by the portfolio `NOTICE.md`; its metrics are not
real-model validation.

## Committed real artifact

Real mode loads [scored-backtest.parquet](scored-backtest.parquet), a 120,000-row deterministic
sample from the 1,347,681-row UCM-curated Lending Club granting archive. It contains disjoint
72,000 train / 24,000 isotonic-calibration / 24,000 later-backtest rows, observed final outcomes,
offline logistic/XGBoost scores, and three directional SHAP reason codes per application.

- Authority: [Zenodo record 11295916](https://zenodo.org/records/11295916)
- DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.11295916](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11295916)
- Retrieval date: 2026-07-17
- License: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

- Authority: [Zenodo record 11295916](https://zenodo.org/records/11295916)
- DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.11295916](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11295916)
- Retrieval date: 2026-07-17
- License: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- Pipeline: [reproduction and locked inputs](../../../pipelines/credit-backtest/README.md)
- Provenance: [source, transport, attribution, and output hashes](../../../pipelines/credit-backtest/PROVENANCE.md)

Raw source rows, direct IDs, ZIP, title, and description are not committed. Published identifiers
are deterministic pseudonyms: linkable within the artifact and dictionary-linkable by a holder of
the public source, not anonymous. The exact output-schema gate, 95 MiB browser budget, time split,
score bounds, outcome types, and reason-code contract fail closed.

## Modeling and claim boundaries

- Baseline: L2-regularized logistic regression; challenger: depth-4 XGBoost. Both use nine disclosed
  application-time source features and are independently isotonic-calibrated on the calibration
  window. Score columns retain float64 precision; all reported model metrics use the later backtest
  window and are computed after rereading the final Parquet.
- EAD is requested amount. LGD is a disclosed 45% assumption. Legacy browser fields absent from the
  archive use explicit unavailable sentinels and do not enter either model.
- Observed swap-set default rates describe the loaded outcome window; they do not prove challenger
  superiority.
- The archive contains granted loans only. Rejected applicants and acceptance-population policy
  effects are not represented. Home-ownership slices are descriptive and are not fairness evidence.

The generated [backtest report](backtest-report.json) and
[methods evidence](methods-evidence.json) are hash-linked to the committed Parquet. This case study
recomputes AUC, Brier, log-loss, and default rate from those exact serialized columns during

validation, deployed accuracy, or real-world fairness.

"modeling": {
    "en": [
      "Baseline: L2-regularized logistic regression over scaled numeric and one-hot categorical application-time features.",
      "Nine source features enter both models: log reported income, capped DTI, log requested amount, FICO, entity-experience flag, employment months, purpose, home ownership, and state.",
      "Challenger: 240-tree depth-4 XGBoost; both scores are independently isotonic-calibrated on the calibration window.",
      "Score columns retain float64 precision, and AUC, Brier, log-loss, and default rate are computed after rereading the final Parquet.",
      "Top-three reason codes are the largest absolute per-application XGBoost SHAP contributions and encode whether each contribution increases or decreases PD. EAD is requested amount; LGD is a disclosed 45% assumption.",
      "The legacy display fields utilization, late payments, and bureau age are respectively mapped to requested-amount/income and explicit unavailable sentinels; they are not model inputs."
    ],
    "zh": [
      "Baseline：基于缩放数值特征与 one-hot 申请时点类别特征，拟合 L2 正则逻辑回归。",
      "9 项来源特征同时进入两模型：log 申报收入、截断 DTI、log 申请金额、FICO、机构经验标记、就业月数、用途、住房状态与州。",
      "Challenger：240 棵、深度 4 的 XGBoost；两组分数各自在标定窗口内独立进行保序校准。",
      "分数字段保留 float64 精度，AUC、Brier、log-loss 与违约率均在重新读取最终 Parquet 后计算。",
      "每条申请的前三原因码取 XGBoost SHAP 绝对贡献最大的三个特征，并编码其对 PD 的升降方向。EAD 为申请金额；LGD 系明确披露的 45% 假设。",

    "en": [
      "Train 72,000 / calibration 24,000 / backtest 24,000; time cutoffs end 2015-12 and 2016-10.",
      "Preprocessing and DTI caps fit on train only; isotonic maps fit on calibration only; all reported metrics use later backtest outcomes."
